meta.title: Docs
meta.description: Get started with MCPEmails in minutes. Quick-start guide, tool reference, and example responses for Gmail, Outlook, and IMAP agents.

hero.lead: Connect any email account, paste one URL into an OAuth-capable MCP client and authorize. Clients without OAuth use an API key instead. Full tool reference and connection guide below.

quickstart.heading: Up and running in minutes.
quickstart.sub: No SDK required. MCPEmails speaks standard MCP over HTTP, so it drops into any MCP-compatible agent.

signup.label: Sign up & connect an inbox
signup.heading: Create your account and connect Gmail
signup.body: Sign up at mcpemails.com, then go to Dashboard → Inboxes → Connect Inbox. Pick Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, or any IMAP inbox, then complete the OAuth flow or paste an app password. Your inbox is ready in under a minute.

apikey.label: Create an API key
apikey.heading: Generate a bearer token for your agent
apikey.body: In Dashboard → API Keys, click "Create key". Name it, select the scopes your agent needs (read:email and/or send:email), and copy the key. It is shown only once.

addclient.label: Add MCPEmails to your agent
addclient.heading: Paste the MCP endpoint into your client
addclient.body: Pick the tab for your client below. MCP clients with OAuth 2.0 support (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) just paste the URL and authorize, no API key needed. Clients without OAuth, plus scripted access, use the API key from step 02.

firstcall.label: Make your first call
firstcall.heading: Ask your agent to check your inbox
firstcall.body: No copy-pasting inbox UUIDs. Your agent calls list_inboxes first to discover every connected inbox and its UUID, then you ask: "Check my inbox and summarise the last 5 unread messages."

endpoint.heading: One URL, standard MCP.
endpoint.sub: All traffic goes to a single Streamable HTTP endpoint. Authenticate with a bearer token from your dashboard.
endpoint.bodyMethods: Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request body. Supported methods: initialize, tools/list, tools/call.

oauth.heading: Zero-config for OAuth-capable clients.
oauth.sub: MCP clients that support OAuth 2.0 (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) connect automatically via authorization code + PKCE. No API key, no config file. Paste the URL and click Connect.
oauth.step1: Step 1: Go to claude.ai → Customize → Connectors → Add connector
oauth.step3: Step 3: Click Connect. MCPEmails opens an authorization screen
oauth.step4: Step 4: Sign in with your mcpemails account and approve access
oauth.stepDone: Done: All six tools are live. claude.ai refreshes tokens automatically
oauth.howTitle: How it works under the hood
oauth.howP1: claude.ai registers itself via RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, so you never pre-register a client ID.
oauth.howP2: Authorization uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636), so no client secret is ever transmitted.
oauth.howP3: Tokens are scoped to exactly the permissions you approve: read:email and/or send:email.
oauth.noOauthNote: Using a client without OAuth support? Create an API key in Dashboard → API Keys and pass it as a bearer token. API key and OAuth connections use the same MCP endpoint and the same six tools.

tools.heading: Six tools. All the email ops your agent needs.
tools.sub: Start with list_inboxes to discover available inboxes and their UUIDs. The remaining five tools each take an inbox_id returned by that call. Click "Show example" to see a full request and response.
tools.noParams: No parameters. Call with an empty arguments object:

list_inboxes.title: List Inboxes
list_inboxes.desc: Returns all inboxes the current API key or OAuth token can access. Call this first to discover inbox_id values, so you never copy-paste UUIDs from the dashboard.

list_inbox.title: List Inbox
list_inbox.desc: List email summaries from a connected inbox, newest first. Supports pagination, folder selection, and unread filtering.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to list. Call list_inboxes first to discover available inbox IDs.
params.limit: Max results to return. Default 20, max 100.
params.folder: Folder to list. Default "INBOX". Other values: "SENT", "DRAFTS", "TRASH".
params.unread_only: Return only unread messages. Default false.

read_email.title: Read Email
read_email.desc: Fetch the full content of a single email by ID, including plain-text body, optional sanitized HTML, and optional attachment data.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox containing the email. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID from list_inbox or search_emails.
params.include_html: Include sanitized HTML body. Default false.
params.include_attachments: Include base64 attachment data. Default false.
params.mark_as_read: Mark message as read after fetching. Default false.

search_emails.title: Search Emails
search_emails.desc: Search an inbox using provider-native query syntax. Gmail supports Gmail search operators; Outlook uses $search; Fastmail and IMAP inboxes use text search.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to search. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.query: Search query. For Gmail: "from:alice@example.com after:2026/01/01". For Outlook: natural-language or KQL queries.
params.include_folders: Restrict search to these folder names. Default: search all folders.

send_email.title: Send Email
send_email.desc: Send a new email from a connected inbox. Supports plain text, optional HTML body, CC/BCC, and file attachments (up to 10 MB total).

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.subject: Email subject line. Max 998 characters.
params.html_body: HTML version of the body (multipart/alternative). Caller is responsible for safe HTML.
params.attachments: File attachments. Each item: '{' filename, mime_type, data (base64) '}'. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

reply_to_email.title: Reply to Email
reply_to_email.desc: Send a reply to an existing email. Threading headers (In-Reply-To, References) are set automatically. Supports reply-all and attachments.

params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that contains the original message. Call list_inboxes to get available inbox IDs.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the email being replied to.
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the reply.
params.reply_all: Reply to all original recipients (To + Cc). Default false.
params.attachments: File attachments. Same schema as send_email. Max 20 items.

errors.heading: Error codes & retry guidance.
errors.sub: Auth, scope, and rate limit failures return a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code. Tool execution failures (inbox not found, provider error, etc.) return a normal result with isError: true and a human-readable message in content[0].text.

rows.auth: Missing, malformed, revoked, or expired API key. Also returned when the API key lacks the required scope for the called tool.
rows.method: Unknown JSON-RPC method (e.g. calling a method other than initialize, tools/list, tools/call)
rows.param: Unknown tool name, or missing / invalid parameter in tools/call
rows.rate: Per-key rate limit or plan daily quota exceeded. Check data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" vs "quota_exceeded". Check data.retry_after (seconds) before retrying.
rows.tool: Tool executed but encountered an error (inbox not found, message not found, provider auth failure, invalid recipient, attachment too large, provider 5xx). The error description is in content[0].text.

rateLimits.heading: Rate limits & quotas.
rateLimits.perKeyBody: Enforced per API key regardless of plan. When exceeded, the server returns error code -32029 with data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" and a data.retry_after field (seconds). Respect that value before retrying.
rateLimits.planHeading: Free 60 / min · Solo 300 / min · Team 1,000 / min
rateLimits.planBody: Usage is unlimited; this is a per-workspace fair-use burst limit (aggregated across all your API keys). When exceeded, calls return data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" with data.window: "per_minute" and a data.retry_after countdown (seconds). Upgrade your plan for a higher ceiling.
rateLimits.retryHeading: Always honour retry_after; never retry sends blindly
rateLimits.retryBody: For rate_limit_exceeded errors, wait data.retry_after seconds before retrying. Use exponential backoff for provider_error. Do not auto-retry send_email on provider_error, since the message may have already been accepted by the provider.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Start on the Free plan: unlimited, no card required. Upgrade to Solo or Team for higher burst limits and team features.

meta.title: Provider Support
meta.description: See which email providers MCPEmails supports and which features are available per provider: Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP.

hero.heading: What works, per provider.
hero.lead: MCPEmails connects Gmail, Outlook, Fastmail, and any IMAP inbox (iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, generic). Not every provider exposes the same APIs — this table shows exactly what each one supports today.

legend.imapNote: iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP all run through the same Deno IMAP/SMTP transport and share identical capabilities. The columns are shown separately for clarity but their feature set is identical.

notes.gmail: Gmail — folders vs labels: Gmail uses a flat label system rather than hierarchical folders. "Move" is implemented as label add/remove. Native copy is not available via the Gmail REST API.
notes.permanentDelete: Permanent delete: Gmail and Outlook move to Trash when you delete — permanent expunge is not exposed by their APIs. IMAP providers (Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, Generic) support both trash and hard expunge.
notes.contacts: Native contacts API: Gmail uses the Google People API; Outlook uses Microsoft Graph /contacts. Fastmail CardDAV and IMAP-based contacts are out of scope for v0.1.
notes.contacts_db: Contact search (DB-synced): All providers automatically populate a contacts table from From, To, and Reply-To headers seen during read, search, and send operations. Use search_contacts and get_contact to query it.
notes.scheduling: Scheduling: Supported for all providers via a server-side scheduled_sends queue. Use schedule_send, list_scheduled, and cancel_scheduled. Delivery uses each provider's existing send path — no provider-native scheduling API is required.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Free plan: unlimited connections, no card required.
